title: An Ionic Dysprosium Complex Made of a Hexanuclear Dy6 Cationic Cluster and a Mononuclear Dy Anionic Unit

material_class.structural_family: ionic Dy6 2,4M6-1 cationic cluster plus mononuclear Dy anion

synthesis.procedure: To a mixture of LH3 (0.23 g, 1.0×10−3 mol) and Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.44 g, 1.0×10−3 mol) in dmf (10 mL) was added piperidine (0.30 g, 3.5×10−3 mol). The resulting solution was heated for 20 min, then left to cool while stirring, filtered, and set aside. Yellow crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction appeared one month later from the dmf solution. The ligand LH3 was prepared separately from butanedione monoxime and 2-hydroxybenzhydrazide in iPrOH. The discussion notes an open atmosphere and excess base/water as favouring carbonate and hydroxo formation.
synthesis.temperature: heated 20 min, then cooled to ambient; crystals after one month
synthesis.time: 20 min heating; crystals after one month
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution synthesis in dmf, open atmosphere; slow crystallization from the filtrate
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: solution heated, cooled while stirring, filtered, and set aside; crystals suitable for XRD formed from the dmf solution after one month

properties.summary: dc χMT of the Dy7 ionic salt is 93.48 cm3 mol−1 K at 300 K (expected 99.20 cm3 mol−1 K for seven isolated DyIII), nearly constant to 100 K, then decreases to 81.27 cm3 mol−1 K at 2 K. Magnetization does not saturate. ac susceptibility is frequency-dependent, suggesting SMM behaviour, but χ″ shows no maxima above 2 K even under 0.1 or 0.2 T dc bias; a bump is attributed to quantum tunnelling. Magellan electrostatic modelling shows poorly aligned Dy anisotropy axes in the Dy6 cation, explaining the limited overall anisotropy.
